message.content: {"caption":"Annotated shopping-search screenshot showing an overloaded headphone search, irrelevant results, and suggested ways to improve the agent’s retrieval.","description":"The left side is an online-shopping results page. Its search field, outlined in red, contains “Bluetooth headphones Sony”; a second red outline highlights the results count, shown as “Items 1–12 of 5758.” Red text over the results says “Too many items to browse.” A narrow sidebar contains shopping options and category filters, while the main area shows four headphone product cards with product images, small descriptions, ratings, prices, and blue Add to Cart buttons; most listing text is too small to read. The thumbnails show several over-ear headphones, and the fourth listing also includes accessories. Lower in the results, a red outline marks a black rectangular item, with the red label “Irrelevant objects” beside it; another similar black item is visible nearby. No arrows or check/cross marks are shown. On the right, “Diagnose the trajectory:” introduces the statement that the agent spent endless steps on “page next,” exhausting interaction limits without providing the requested information. Below a horizontal divider, “Distilled strategies to ReasoningBank:” lists search-query optimization to avoid irrelevance and improve precision, adjusting the number of items displayed per page to accelerate browsing, and using available filters.","figure_type":"screenshot","chart_values":[]}
